score_rationale: Exceptional willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial B2B database market with at least 8 major vendors currently selling comprehensive trucking and logistics company databases: US Trucking Companies (4.2M+ carrier records with emails, phones, fleet data at $399 for complete CSV download), Openmart (150,000+ verified trucking company owner emails with 97% data accuracy and monthly updates), DataCaptive (417,000+ verified trucking executives and professionals), Scrap.io (86,607+ US trucking businesses verified), Data Masters (400,000+ trucking companies with email addresses, 99% with phone numbers available), CampaignLake (217,000+ transportation industry verified contacts), Averick Media (53,741+ trucking company records), and Blue Mail Media (95% deliverable trucking fleet owner data). Commercial vendors report 95-97% data accuracy with monthly to quarterly updates and 85-95% email deliverability rates, indicating robust market demand. One vendor (US Trucking Companies) explicitly prices complete dataset at $399, establishing transparent baseline significantly above DataStructured's typical $79-$149 wedge price point while still affordable enough to validate strong small/mid-market demand. Four exceptionally high-value B2B buyer segments with massive LTV justification: (1) Transportation Management Systems and fleet management software vendors (Samsara fleet tracking and ELD compliance platform at $35-$75/vehicle/month = $4,200-$9,000/year for 10-truck fleet, Motive AI dashcams and fleet management at $30-$60/vehicle/month, KeepTruckin ELD and compliance, Omnitracs fleet optimization, McLeod LoadMaster TMS for brokers, TMW.Suite for carriers, PeopleNet fleet management) selling SaaS subscriptions at $2,000-$50,000/year per trucking company depending on fleet size, generating $20,000-$500,000 LTV per customer over 10-year relationship where one acquired fleet justifies $5,000-$10,000 CAC making $149 database deliver 34×-67× cost savings; (2) Electronic Logging Device (ELD) hardware and compliance vendors (Garmin eLog ELD devices at $495+ per truck, Rand McNally ELD tablets, Omnitracs IVG, Geotab GO devices, Verizon Connect ELD) selling FMCSA-mandated ELD hardware at $300-$800 per truck plus $20-$40/month data plans to 500,000+ trucking companies (ELD mandate covers all carriers operating commercial vehicles in interstate commerce), generating $3,600-$9,600 per 10-truck fleet annually where one fleet sale covers database cost 24×-64×; (3) Freight factoring and financial services companies (RTS Financial invoice factoring at 1.5-5% of gross freight bill value, OTR Capital advance funding, Triumph Business Capital, Porter Freight Funding) providing cash flow financing to owner-operators and small fleets where factoring one carrier hauling $50,000/month generates $750-$2,500/month in factoring fees ($9,000-$30,000/year), making one client acquisition worth 60×-200× database cost; and (4) Commercial trucking insurance brokers and underwriters (Progressive Commercial truck insurance, Berkshire Hathaway GUARD, Northland Insurance, CoverWallet commercial auto) selling required liability insurance, cargo insurance, and physical damage coverage at $8,000-$25,000/year premiums for owner-operators and $50,000-$500,000/year for medium/large fleets (10-100+ trucks), with insurance brokers earning standard 10-15% commissions generating $800-$75,000/year per placed policy where one fleet client justifies 5×-500× database investment. Secondary buyer segments include: diesel fuel card providers (Comdata, EFS, WEX fuel cards offering 10-50 cents/gallon discounts generating $5,000-$30,000/year in transaction fees per fleet), truck dealerships (Freightliner, Kenworth, Peterbilt, Volvo, International selling Class 8 semi-trucks at $150,000-$200,000 each), parts suppliers (brakes, tires, filters, DEF fluid), maintenance software, load board subscriptions, and freight broker technology. Massive total addressable market: approximately 500,000-550,000 for-hire trucking companies registered with FMCSA operating in interstate commerce (per FMCSA census data), plus 350,000-400,000 additional private fleet carriers (Walmart fleet, food service distributors, construction material haulers), for combined 850,000-950,000 total trucking operations in US. Within for-hire segment: 95% are small carriers with 1-10 trucks (owner-operators and micro-fleets), 3% are 11-100 trucks (small/medium fleets), and 2% are 100+ trucks (large carriers and national LTL networks like Old Dominion, XPO, Estes Express). This creates 500,000-600,000 total prospect companies with 1,000,000-1,500,000 decision-maker contacts (owner-operators, fleet managers, safety directors, operations VPs, CFOs at larger carriers). Excellent public data availability: FMCSA Company Snapshot database (safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/CompanySnapshot.aspx) is federally mandated public registry containing USDOT number, legal name, DBA, physical address, mailing address, phone, email (where provided), MC/FF/MX authority numbers, insurance status, safety rating, fleet size, cargo carried, operation class (interstate/intrastate/both), out-of-service rates, inspections, crashes, and violations for every registered carrier — 100% public under FOIA with zero authentication barriers and daily updates. Additional data from state commercial vehicle registrations (heavy truck registration databases), SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) directory, and DOT MCS-150 biennial updates. Engineering lift is low-to-moderate: bulk download or API scrape FMCSA Company Census (public bulk data available), parse carrier classification (for-hire vs. private, LTL vs. truckload vs. specialized), geocode addresses, normalize fleet size buckets (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11-20, 21-50, 51-100, 100+), classify cargo types (general freight, refrigerated, flatbed, tanker, auto haulers, household goods), flag active insurance and operating authority status, append email addresses where missing via business directory lookups. Strong flat-file competitor validation: US Trucking Companies sells 4.2M+ records at $399, establishing that market will pay $399 for comprehensive dataset, creating massive wedge opportunity at $149 for DataStructured to undercut by 63% while still maintaining strong margins. Openmart's 150K records with 97% accuracy and monthly updates demonstrates sustained enterprise demand. Score is 8 due to: (a) exceptionally strong validated commercial vendor ecosystem with 8+ active vendors and transparent pricing data point at $399 for 4M+ records, (b) ultra-high buyer LTV across four primary segments (fleet software $20K-$500K LTV, ELD hardware $3,600-$9,600/year recurring, freight factoring $9K-$30K/year, insurance $800-$75K/year in broker commissions) where one customer acquisition justifies 5×-3,300× database cost, (c) massive TAM (850K-950K trucking companies generating 1M-1.5M decision-maker contacts), (d) excellent public data availability via FMCSA federally mandated registry with daily updates and zero authentication barriers, (e) low-to-moderate engineering complexity due to centralized federal database, and (f) strong wedge pricing opportunity ($149 undercuts $399 competitor by 63% for comparable or superior dataset). Score not higher than 8 due to: (a) existing competitor already offers comprehensive dataset at accessible $399 price point (though DataStructured can still undercut significantly), and (b) high market fragmentation with 95% of carriers being micro-fleets (1-10 trucks) creates mix of high-value targets (medium/large fleets) and lower-value long-tail (owner-operators), though even owner-operators represent strong buyers for ELD, factoring, and insurance products with $10,000-$50,000 annual spending.

A one-time $149 CSV undercuts US Trucking Companies' $399 dataset by 63% while delivering comparable 500K-900K records from same federal FMCSA source, targeting fleet software vendors, ELD providers, factoring companies, insurance brokers, fuel card providers, truck dealers, and freight technology platforms serving capital-intensive $800B US trucking industry.

data_wanted: FMCSA Company Snapshot database (safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/CompanySnapshot.aspx) is the authoritative federally mandated public registry containing all for-hire motor carriers, private carriers (in some cases), brokers, freight forwarders, and cargo tank facilities operating in interstate commerce — 100% public under Freedom of Information Act with zero authentication barriers, searchable by USDOT number or company name, with daily updates as carriers file MCS-150 biennial updates and authority applications. Bulk data available via FMCSA public data downloads or API scraping. Key fields per carrier record: USDOT number (unique federal identifier assigned to all carriers), MC number (Motor Carrier operating authority for for-hire carriers), FF number (Freight Forwarder authority), MX number (Mexico-domiciled carrier authority), legal business name and DBA/trade name, physical address (terminal/headquarters location), mailing address, phone number, email address (where provided by carrier in federal filing), entity type (Corporation, LLC, Partnership, Sole Proprietorship), operation classification (Authorized For-Hire, Private [Property], Private [Passenger], Exempt For-Hire), carrier operation (Interstate, Intrastate Hazmat, Intrastate Non-Hazmat), cargo carried via checkboxes (General Freight, Household Goods, Metal: sheets/coils/rolls, Motor Vehicles, Drive/Tow Away, Logs/Poles/Beams/Lumber, Building Materials, Mobile Homes, Machinery Large Objects, Fresh Produce, Liquids/Gases, Intermodal Containers, Passengers, Oil Field Equipment, Livestock, Grain/Feed/Hay, Coal/Coke, Meat, Garbage/Refuse/Trash, US Mail, Chemicals, Commodities Dry Bulk, Refrigerated Food, Beverages, Paper Products, Utilities, Agricultural/Farm Supplies, Construction, Water Well, other), HAZMAT flag (yes/no), passenger carrier flag, out-of-service date (if applicable), total power units (truck and tractor count), total drivers, MCS-150 form date (biennial update), MCS-150 mileage (annual miles driven), insurance carrier name, policy number, insurance status, SCAC code (4-letter Standard Carrier Alpha Code for EDI transactions), safety rating (Satisfactory, Conditional, Unsatisfactory, Not Rated), safety review date, out-of-service rate (percentage of vehicle inspections resulting in OOS), vehicle inspections count (last 24 months), driver inspections, total violations, crash total, injury crashes, fatality crashes, tow-away crashes, and state of domicile. Target all active carriers (exclude only carriers with revoked authority or long-term out-of-service status) across all cargo types and fleet sizes. FMCSA database contains approximately 500,000-550,000 active for-hire interstate carriers, 80,000-100,000 active freight brokers, plus subset of private carriers (400,000+ additional private fleets exist but not all required to register unless crossing state lines with hazmat). Target output: 600,000-700,000 total rows covering for-hire carriers, brokers, and registered private fleets. Additional data enrichment: Cross-reference USDOT numbers with state commercial vehicle registration databases (CDL and heavy truck registration records), append SCAC directory data, enrich missing email addresses via business directory lookups (YellowPages, Google Business, ZoomInfo) and domain pattern matching (info@carriernamedotcom, dispatch@carriernamedotcom), classify fleet size buckets (1 truck owner-operator, 2-5 trucks micro-fleet, 6-10 trucks small fleet, 11-20 trucks small-medium, 21-50 trucks medium, 51-100 trucks large, 100+ trucks major carrier), geocode for regional targeting. Data is 100% public: FMCSA registry is federal public record under 49 USC § 13908 requiring disclosure of motor carrier operating authority information, with carrier contact details, fleet size, cargo types, insurance status, and safety ratings fully disclosed in Company Snapshot system without any authentication or paid access requirements — API and bulk download access confirmed available for automated data collection.

One acquired 50-truck fleet paying $40,000/year = 268× ROI vs. database cost. (2) ELD hardware vendors: FMCSA ELD mandate creates captive market of 500,000+ carriers required to equip 3.5M+ Class 7-8 trucks. Hardware $300-$800/truck plus $20-$40/month data plans. 10-truck fleet = $3,000-$8,000 upfront + $2,400-$4,800/year recurring = $3,600-$9,600 first year, $30,000-$80,000 LTV. One fleet = 24×-64× ROI. Medium fleet (25 trucks, $200,000/year premium) = $20,000-$30,000/year commission = 134×-200× ROI. One large fleet client = 500×-5,000× ROI. US Trucking Companies' $399 pricing for 4.2M records establishes transparent willingness-to-pay baseline — market clearly pays $399 for comprehensive FMCSA dataset. DataStructured wedge at $149 undercuts by 63% while offering comparable or superior dataset from same federal source. Openmart's 97% accuracy and monthly updates demonstrates enterprise buyers pay premium for data quality. Massive TAM (850K-950K carriers, 1M-1.5M decision-makers) combined with mandatory regulatory spending (ELD mandate, insurance requirements) and capital-intensive operations ($150K-$200K per new Class 8 truck, $50K/year fuel costs per truck, $8K-$500K/year insurance) creates exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay across all four primary buyer segments plus secondary segments (fuel cards, truck dealers, parts, maintenance software).
